novelty_flags.label: thm:joint-system-limit and thm:separate-joint-frontier
novelty_flags.one_line: The survey misses Hsieh2026, a close staggered-DDD preprint that explicitly derives inference accounting for cross-stack dependence from reused comparison units; it does not subsume joint GMM, but must be compared theorem-by-theorem.

soundness_flags.label: def:joint-estimator and thm:joint-system-limit
soundness_flags.one_line: The stated L2 nuisance-rate condition permits fitted cell propensities equal to zero, and the empirical covariance can be singular, so the displayed score ratios and inverse-weight loadings need not define a statistic; the Wald interval is likewise unspecified.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:joint-system-limit / technical_internal_limitation
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Optimality is only over constant loadings in the fixed finite-dimensional span of the retained pairwise DDD scores, not the full semiparametric DDD model.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The headline is score-span joint-GMM optimality and inference conditional on fixed T, target support, retained comparisons, and prespecified aggregation weights.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper identifies ATT(g,t) with any clean not-yet-treated comparison, permits weights summing to one across those comparisons, and interprets the resulting within-(g,t) combination as optimal GMM using recentered influence functions.

The paper gives closed-form efficient influence functions for staggered-DiD and event-study parameters using multiple comparison groups and periods, then proposes an attaining nonparametric estimator.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 8-11, Theorems 5 and 7 and equations (6) and (8)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper derives efficient influence functions for canonical panel and repeated-cross-section DDD settings and specifies cross-fitted nuisance estimation.
The article studies semiparametric two-step GMM with nuisance functions and states that optimally weighted two-step GMM can attain the semiparametric efficiency bound in its general model.
The cited article establishes consistency and asymptotic normality for estimators based on sample analogues of population orthogonality conditions.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 57(298), 1962
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article applies system-wide generalized least squares and reports asymptotic efficiency gains relative to equation-by-equation least squares under practically occurring conditions.
The article formalizes the triple-difference estimand and its identifying parallel-trends logic, including its relation to a difference of two DiD estimators.

source_verification_receipts.locator: journal record; accepted-manuscript discussion of Assumption 3.2 and equations (3.44)-(3.45)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited DML work uses Neyman-orthogonal scores and cross-fitting; its smooth-problem discussion identifies o(N^-1/4) as a crude sufficient nuisance-rate requirement.

This public preprint develops stacked staggered DDD and explicitly states that unit-level variance aggregation accounts for cross-stack dependence caused by reused comparison units; it presents itself as complementary to GMM rather than deriving joint GMM optimality.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define a feasible learner class with propensity clipping or another explicit positivity-preserving map, an eventual invertibility condition or regularized inverse for the sample covariance, and the exact studentized Wald interval.

Add Hsieh2026 to related work and state a direct comparison theorem: isolate how the proposed joint GMM changes the shared-unit covariance treatment relative to stacked DDD's valid but non-optimal aggregation.

Strengthen the field contribution with a DDD-realizable, nondegenerate family of reuse graphs and laws yielding a strictly positive, observable lower bound on the joint-versus-separate variance gain; retain the GLS identity as its corollary.

recommended_next_step: Revise the feasible estimator into a defined statistic and add the missed stacked-DDD comparator before advancing this field-tier score-span efficiency angle.
